No issues.

I found no added line that breaks a quotable rule in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agents/domain.md`, `GLOSSARY.md` or the ADRs I checked.

- **Code comments:** the added comments in `claude-default-settings.service` and `smoke.sh` each state a reason the code can't show.
  - The `Before=` comment explains why the unit must run before pre-approval and remote control.
  - The `cp, not install` comment explains why `cp` writes through a symlink.
  - The shellcheck disable names the cause, jq's own `$d`.
- **Glossary:** `Claude default settings` follows the existing entry format, with a definition and an `_Avoid_` line. It has no implementation detail. The PR uses that term and doesn't drift to the avoided synonyms.
- **ADRs:**
  - ADR 0012 (nothing under a home directory) isn't contradicted. The unit writes the settings at each start rather than baking them into `/home/dev`, which is the approach the PR body gives for working around that ADR.
  - No ADR is superseded, so there is nothing to delete.
- **PR text:** the body lists no files and contains no diffs.

**Dismissed for human review.** The new `images/coder-template/claude-default-settings.json` largely duplicates the repository's own `.claude/settings.json`, which could be read as against "YAGNI, KISS, DRY." I dropped it. The two files serve different consumers (this repo's Claude sessions versus every workspace user), and the rule text doesn't say they must share a source. It would not block either way.

No issues.

I checked these against the head commit:

- **Ordering:** `claude-default-settings.service` is `Before=` both `claude-pre-approval.service` and `claude-remote-control.service`. The target `Wants=` all three, so the copy lands first. The pre-approval step then adds `enableAllProjectMcpServers` through `merge`. `merge` resolves the symlink with `readlink -f` and writes the real file.
- **Restarts:** `claude-remote-control.service` restarts alone because of `Restart=always`. The defaults unit has `RemainAfterExit` and `PartOf` the target, so it doesn't rerun or clobber the pre-approval key on those restarts.
- **Symlink:** `cp` writes through a symlinked `~/.claude/settings.json` and leaves the link in place. The smoke test checks the target's content and that the link is still a link.
- **Smoke coverage:**
  - The symlink case asserts the target equals the defaults plus the pre-approval key. That also proves the user's `model: smoke` is overwritten.
  - The fresh-home case asserts `cmp` equality with the defaults.
  - The trust-off case asserts `enableAllProjectMcpServers` is absent.

The one behavioral shift is that a restart with trust switched off now drops a previously written `enableAllProjectMcpServers`. That is the documented overwrite behavior and the PR description discloses it, so it isn't a defect. I'm not raising it.

No issues.

I checked every added line in GLOSSARY.md, docs/usage/coder-template.md, the comments in `claude-default-settings.service`, and the comment in smoke.sh. None records provenance, a defended alternative, or dated tool behavior.

| Anchor | Quoted text | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GLOSSARY.md` › "Claude default settings" | "taking precedence over the user's own" | KEEP | The service copies the file over `~/.claude/settings.json` at each start. Smoke.sh asserts the result. |
| `docs/usage/coder-template.md` | "so a change made there lasts only until the next start; `~/.claude.json` and project settings are untouched" | KEEP | This states a constraint. `claude-default-settings.service@ExecStart` writes only `~/.claude/settings.json`. |
| `claude-default-settings.service` | "Claude pre-approval adds to the same file, and remote control must start with the defaults in place." | KEEP | The `Before=` line on the next line encodes it. Smoke.sh checks that pre-approval's `enableAllProjectMcpServers` coexists with the defaults. |
| `claude-default-settings.service` | "cp, not install: it writes through a symlinked file (a dotfiles checkout's, say) instead of replacing the link." | KEEP | This is a load-bearing prohibition, not a dead alternative. Smoke.sh asserts the symlink survives (`readlink ... ../dotfiles/settings.json`) and that the target holds the defaults. |
| `smoke.sh` | "# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # jq's own $d" | KEEP | It states why a lint suppression is needed. |

I made no edits.

review.body: No issues found. The title and description match the change. The new user unit copies the Claude default settings over `~/.claude/settings.json` before Claude pre-approval and remote control start, and `cp` writes through a dotfiles symlink without replacing the link. The smoke test now covers both the symlinked case and a fresh home. The new glossary entry and the usage-doc note agree with ADR 0012 and ADR 0016.
